reviews.one_line_contribution: A matched-volume decoupled-collection control (grow the bank from memory-OFF episodes) that tries to relocate the cause of self-evolving-memory degradation from what gets written to whether the writing episodes were conditioned on retrieval, crossed 2x2 with a reflective prompt optimizer plus an instruction/bank transplant to test whether the contraction co-adapts into the evolved instruction.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The proposal names CoEvo-Mem (2608.01739) and handles it well, but the sharper threat is the model-collapse cluster it cites only as 'formalism.' Alemohammad et al. already establish fresh-data mixing ratio as the knob, which is exactly M50 -- the 'one-line fix' is a transplant, not a discovery. More damaging, the accumulate-vs-replace result (Gerstgrasser et al. 2024) shows recursive degradation is driven by *replacement*, and an append-only memory bank is pure accumulation; that literature therefore predicts the null (A1 ~ A2) unless retrieval competition at k=4 supplies the selection pressure that replacement supplies in the training case. The proposal asserts the transplant 'is not entailed' but never engages the one prior result that specifically predicts its refutation condition. Separately, ExpeL-style pipelines commonly bootstrap insight extraction from unconditioned trajectories, so A2 is closer to existing practice than the framing ('the standard self-evolving loop' = A1) admits; a reviewer may read A1, not A2, as the constructed arm.
reviews.strongest_objection: The two arms that carry the paper's practical message are the least powered in the study, and the predictions attached to them are stated below the design's own stated resolution. Measurement says non-core arms (2 seeds) 'support only ~7-8 point contrasts,' yet Prediction 4 demands that B2's tail accuracy sit *within 3 points* of A1 (a 3-point equivalence claim at an 7-8 point MDE -- uncertifiable), and Prediction 5 demands M50 recover 'two-thirds of the A1->A2 tail gap,' i.e. ~4 points of a gap the *core, 3-seed* contrast can only detect at 5-6 points. So 'content gating does not rescue' and 'mixing works' are both unfalsifiable as written, and the headline deployable fix (M50) is a 2-seed arm evaluated once. Compounding this, B2 and B3 break the design's central invariant: the paper claims 'bank size trajectories are identical across arms by construction,' but a verification/self-consistency gate and a coverage gate reject writes by definition. Either they write fewer than 40 items per cycle -- reintroducing the exact bank-size confound F0 exists to control -- or candidates are resampled until 40 pass, which converts both gates into re-rankers with different semantics from the EDV/ConsistencyGate methods they are meant to instantiate. Since B2 is named as 'the most likely way the hypothesis dies,' a competing baseline that is neither size-matched nor faithfully implemented cannot arbitrate anything. Two further defects: (i) metric (b), retrieval-count Gini 'accumulated during collection,' is undefined for A2 and A4, whose collecting episodes have no retrieval at all -- Prediction 2's claim that 'A2 stays flat' is vacuous on that metric; (ii) the mediation analysis regresses instance-level tail correctness on effective rank and cluster coverage, which are bank-level quantities taking one value per arm-seed-cycle and are collinear with arm identity, so 'entering contraction metrics attenuates the deficit by half' is close to guaranteed by construction and is arm-indicator laundering, not mechanism evidence.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Move B2, B3 and M50 to 3 seeds (they are ~4.8k episodes, well inside the stated envelope after cutting the redundant cycle-2 evaluation and the 1,600 null-replicate episodes), or restate Predictions 4 and 5 at the resolution the arms actually support and say so up front. 2) Specify the gate protocol explicitly: resample distillation candidates until 40 pass, report rejection rates, and add a size-matched no-gate control so B2/B3 remain comparable to A1. 3) Redefine the retrieval-concentration metric on the fixed 300-query probe set (a counterfactual retrieval trace computable for every arm) rather than on collection-time retrievals, which do not exist in decoupled arms. 4) Fix the optimizer confound: A4's optimizer evolves instructions against memory-OFF failure traces but is deployed with k=4 memory, so it is optimized under a condition it never sees -- a standard train/deploy mismatch that predicts A4 instructions underperform for reasons unrelated to contraction, and it sits on the wrong side of Prediction 7. Add the missing cell (optimizer evolves on memory-ON episodes over a decoupled-grown bank) to separate bank provenance from the optimizer's evaluation condition. 5) Replace the pooled mediation with within-arm variation (across seeds and cycles, arm fixed) or drop the mediation claim. 6) Report one larger-bank condition (bank growth is cheap; only evaluation is not) so the mechanism is not established solely in a 160-item, k=4 regime chosen because contraction is measurable there.
reviews.missing_baseline: An injection-budget arm. The track's own established starting result is that *volume* was the causal lever -- cutting injection from seven items to three eliminated the harm from the same bank -- and this design freezes k=4 at every evaluation in every arm. A contracted bank at fixed k delivers more mutually redundant context than a diverse bank at the same k, so 'narrower support' and 'more redundant injected content' are perfectly confounded, and the single most likely alternative explanation in this literature is untested. A cycle-3 k-sweep (k=1/2/4) on A1 and A2 banks would separate them and costs only evaluation episodes. Also missing, as above, the 2x2's fifth cell: optimizer evolved on memory-conditioned episodes over a decoupled bank, without which A3-vs-A4 is not a clean manipulation of the optimizer channel.
reviews.preprint_collision: Above average for this genre and not padded: it names CoEvo-Mem as a near-identical mechanistic premise, refuses to minimize it, explicitly states that a reviewer may read prong 1 as 'testing CoEvo-Mem's premise adversarially,' and pre-commits to a fallback if a decoupled-collection ablation appears in CoEvo-Mem's camera-ready. The admitted gap (no OpenReview 2026 sweep) is the right one to admit, and it is the live risk: the entire novelty case reduces to 'nobody ran the memory-off collection ablation,' which is precisely the shape of a result that lives in a sibling preprint's appendix, and the proposal itself concedes this. Two real deficiencies. First, the collision check treats the model-collapse cluster as supplying only 'formalism' and never searches it for a competing *prediction*; the accumulate-vs-replace line predicts that append-only stores do not collapse, which directly threatens Prediction 1, and the mixing-ratio result already supplies M50. Novelty against that cluster is asserted by the phrase 'transplanting it is not entailed' rather than searched. Second, the check separates every partial collision (Trap of Trajectory, xMemory, DecentMem, EDV, ConsistencyGate) using the same content-vs-policy distinction that the proposal's own refutation condition (iii) concedes may not survive contact with B3 -- if a write-time diversity gate matches A2, the collisions with the retrieval-redundancy and admission-control lines become substantive rather than partial. I found no preprint that already makes this exact claim, but the novelty margin is thinner than the check presents.

reviews.one_line_contribution: That degradation in self-evolving agent memory is caused by the collection policy — episodes being executed while conditioned on retrieved items, which makes retrieval self-reinforcing and contracts the bank's support — rather than by any property of the written content, demonstrated by a decoupled-collection control (A2) matched on tasks, write path and write count, and extended to a second self-editing channel via a 2x2 with a reflective prompt optimizer plus an instruction/bank transplant.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats, one of which the proposal misses entirely. (a) CoEvo-Mem (cited as arXiv 2608.01739) states the identical structural premise; the proposal is right that it is a competing hypothesis rather than a scoop, but a reviewer can fairly read prong 1 as an adversarial ablation of someone else's stated mechanism, which is a modest contribution frame. (b) The one the proposal never cites and that hurts more: degenerate feedback loops in recommender systems — Jiang, Chiappa, Lattimore, Gyorgy, Kohli, 'Degenerate Feedback Loops in Recommender Systems' (AIES 2019), and Chaney, Stewart, Engelhardt, 'How Algorithmic Confounding in Recommendation Systems Increases Homogeneity' (RecSys 2018), plus the exposure-bias line (Mansoury et al. 2020). Those results already establish, formally and empirically, that a system whose future observations are drawn under its own ranking contracts its effective support via preferential attachment, and that randomizing/injecting exploration restores it. B1 (uniform retrieval) and M50 (mixing) are exactly the known fixes from that literature, as is the fresh-data mixing ratio from the model-collapse work the proposal does cite. So the dynamic, the diagnosis and the remedy are all imported; what is genuinely new is the substrate (an append-only text bank retrieved into a frozen model's context, where no weights are updated) and the crossing with a prompt optimizer. That is a real but incremental delta, and the Related Work's framing of the mechanism as previously unidentified overstates it.
reviews.strongest_objection: A2 is not a control that isolates 'the collection policy' — it differs from A1 on at least two mundane content pathways that alone predict the entire predicted signature (predictions 1-3), and neither is controlled. (i) Textual copying: in A1 the ExpeL-style distiller is fed a trajectory whose context contained the four retrieved items, so a contracting bank is the expected output of ordinary paraphrase, not of preferential attachment; in A2 the distiller never sees them. Metric (d) would detect the redundancy but cannot attribute it. (ii) Write-set composition: W=40 successful episodes are sampled 'uniformly at random' from successes, and memory plausibly raises success rate most on the five head clusters that already take 65% of draws, so A1's writable pool is head-skewed by construction. Equalizing the write *count* (limitation 3) does not equalize the cluster *composition*, and cluster composition is precisely what effective rank, Gini and cluster coverage measure. A1 could therefore satisfy predictions 1, 2 and 3 exactly while the title's causal claim is unsupported. Compounding this, 'collection policy, not content quality' is a false dichotomy on its face: collection policy has no channel to the bank except through written content, so the identifiable question is only correctness-gating versus diversity-gating — and the proposal's own arm B3 is a content-side diversity gate that is fairly likely to succeed, at which point refutation condition (iii) concedes the deployable recommendation and the paper reduces to 'gate for coverage, not correctness', which the memory-selection literature already does. Second blade: the regime (40-item seed, <=160 items, k=4, 65% draw skew) is admittedly chosen so contraction is 'measurable within three cycles', while the MDE arithmetic gives 5-6 points on the primary A1-vs-A2 tail contrast and 8-10 on the 2x2 interaction — larger than the effects the track's own prior measurements produced (full-bank injection broke 6-7 items; optimizer gains sat inside a 5-14 point re-scoring drift). The design is thus squeezed between power and ecological validity: a positive result shows a regime can be constructed in which the loop contracts, and a null at cycle 3 is uninformative by the authors' own limitation 1.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in priority order. (1) Add a memory-masked-distillation arm: episodes run fully coupled, but the retrieved items are stripped from the distiller's input. This is the arm that separates 'the episode was conditioned on retrieval' from 'the writer paraphrased what it was shown', and without it prong 1's causal claim is not identified. (2) Stratify the W=40 write sample by task cluster (or report cluster-conditional write rates and re-run the contraction metrics on a composition-matched subsample) so that contraction cannot be a pure success-rate selection effect under the skewed draw distribution. (3) Retitle and restate the claim to something the design can actually adjudicate — 'correctness-gated admission does not prevent support contraction; coverage-aware or decoupled collection does' — and treat B3 as a co-primary intervention rather than a threat, since it is the deployable one (A2 is not deployable: it discards memory during collection). (4) Fix the transplant test's confound: A3's and A4's instructions were evolved against different episode distributions, so any tail gap may be generic optimizer/trace quality, not co-adaptation to a contracted support. Add an arm where the optimizer evolves against memory-conditioned episodes over a *frozen* cycle-0 bank; only if A3's instruction underperforms *that* one on a healthy bank is co-adaptation to contraction demonstrated. Also cite and position against the recommender feedback-loop literature explicitly rather than only model collapse. Given the stated 8-10 point interaction MDE, either buy power for the 2x2 (more trajectories, or within-trajectory instruction swaps) or drop it from the abstract and make the corrected transplant the co-adaptation evidence.
reviews.missing_baseline: The coupled-collection / memory-masked-distillation arm (A1 with retrieved items removed from the distiller's context). Reviewers will demand it because it is the only arm that distinguishes preferential attachment through the agent's behaviour from the writer simply copying the text it was shown, and its absence means B2, B3, B1, F0 and M50 all leave the trivial explanation standing. Secondary omissions a reviewer would also raise: a cluster-stratified write-sampling arm (to kill the success-composition confound), and a coupled-instruction / frozen-bank arm (to make the transplant contrast interpretable as co-adaptation rather than trace quality).
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is well above average for this format and should be credited: it names a near-identical mechanistic premise (CoEvo-Mem), refuses to minimize it, converts it into a live outcome as baseline (ii), and flags honestly that it could not sweep OpenReview 2026 and that a memory-off collection ablation could sit in a sibling appendix. That is the right posture. Two real deficiencies remain. First, it reports conclusions but no protocol — no queries, no date windows, no venues, no indication of whether arXiv listings for the last 60-90 days were swept as opposed to keyword search — so 'the literature search run for this revision' is unauditable, and the field's fastest-moving surface (very recent preprints on retrieval-conditioned write-back) is exactly where the risk lives. Second, and more damaging, the search is scoped to agent-memory and model-collapse preprints and misses the older, non-preprint literature that already owns the claim: degenerate feedback loops and algorithmic-confounding homogenization in recommender systems (Jiang et al. AIES 2019; Chaney et al. RecSys 2018), where 'the policy that selects what is observed makes future observations reinforce it, contracting support' is a settled result with randomization/exploration as the established remedy. Likewise the mixing-ratio fix (M50) is presented as this proposal's one-line contribution, but accumulate-versus-replace results in the self-consuming-data line already predict it, and the proposal cites Shumailov and Alemohammad without engaging that specific finding. So: no exact scoop identified, but the novelty claim is narrower than the check concludes — the mechanism and the fix are both prior, and only the substrate and the prompt-optimizer crossing survive.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A matched-volume decoupling experiment claiming that diversity collapse in self-editing agent memory is caused by growing the bank from retrieval-conditioned episodes (the collection policy) rather than by the quality of what is written, plus a 2x2 crossing with a reflective prompt optimizer and an instruction/bank transplant showing the evolved instruction itself absorbs and carries the contraction.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats, in different directions. (a) CoEvo-Mem (arXiv 2608.01739) states the identical structural premise — retrieval determines usage signals, updated bank reshapes retrieval — so the mechanism is already named in print; what remains for this proposal is the sign of the effect and one ablation (a memory-off collection arm), which is a standard control rather than a new idea. The proposal concedes this and it is a fair concession, but the honesty does not restore the novelty. (b) ExpeL-lineage practice is the underrated threat: ExpeL extracts insights from a separately collected training pool, i.e. collection episodes that are not conditioned on the bank being built. Arm A2 is therefore close to earlier standard practice, and M50 (50% memory-off collection) is the fresh-data mixing-ratio knob already established in the model-collapse literature the proposal cites (Shumailov et al.; LLM Web Dynamics). So the diagnostic framing may be new; the proposed intervention is a rediscovery of an older design plus a known knob.
reviews.strongest_objection: The primary contrast, A1 vs A2, cannot arbitrate the proposal's own dichotomy (collection policy vs content), because memory-off collecting episodes produce different trajectories and therefore different written items — content is not held fixed, it is exactly what varies. Every content-side account in the related work predicts prediction 3 (A2 tail exceeds A1 tail by >=6 points) with no appeal to retrieval self-reinforcement: OEP's locally-correct-but-non-transferable experiences and Trap of Trajectory's spurious feature-outcome correlations are both *more* likely in memory-conditioned episodes. B2 is offered as the discriminator, but it gates verification plus self-consistency, i.e. hallucination and inconsistency only; it does not gate spuriousness or non-transferability. So prediction 4's 'B2 tracks A1, not A2' would refute one narrow content account while the abstract and title claim it refutes the content account in general. Second, the write composition is matched only in count. Sampling W=40 successful episodes uniformly means A1 — which by the proposal's own head/tail story succeeds disproportionately on the five large head clusters — writes head-skewed items simply because of where it succeeded. Prediction 2's >=25% cluster-coverage drop and much of the effective-rank decline in prediction 1 then follow mechanically from differential success location, not from preferential attachment in retrieval. The plan never reports, let alone matches, the per-cluster composition of the 40 written items per arm. Third, the compounding half of the title is pre-declared possibly unresolvable: the 2x2 interaction MDE is 8-10 points against a prediction stated at 8, so prong 2 is powered to return 'underpowered' and the transplant test is left carrying it.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Add a write-blinded coupled arm: collecting episodes read memory as in A1, but distillation runs on the trajectory with retrieved items masked out. This is the arm that separates 'memory changed the trajectory' from 'memory contaminated the distillation', which is the actual content/policy split being claimed. (2) Cluster-stratify the write sampling so the per-cluster composition of each cycle's 40 items is matched across A1 and A2, and report per-arm write composition as a first-class table; without it, predictions 1 and 2 are confounded with success location. (3) Add a content-transplant arm — grow a bank from A1's items subsampled to A2's effective rank, and the converse — so the mechanism claim is tested with provenance held fixed; the existing shuffled-provenance placebo only relabels text and does not do this. (4) Establish a null band for the transplant contrast with a within-arm instruction swap (A4 instruction from seed i evaluated on A4 bank from seed j). Prediction 7's 4-point threshold compares instructions produced by two different GEPA runs at 6 candidates per cycle; 4 points is plausibly inside optimizer-seed variance, and nothing in the design bounds that. (5) Actually test preferential attachment — fit retrieval-count growth against current count across cycles — instead of asserting 'rich get richer' and measuring only Gini and effective rank, neither of which distinguishes a self-reinforcing process from a one-shot compositional skew. (6) Broaden B2 to include a non-transferability/spuriousness gate, or stop claiming the content account is refuted.
reviews.missing_baseline: A reduced deployment-time injection-budget arm. The track's established prior result is that cutting injection from seven retrieved items to three eliminated the harm from the *same* bank — volume, not content, was the measured lever. This plan freezes k=4 in every arm at every evaluation and never varies it, so a coupled bank evaluated at k=1-2 is absent. If that cell removes A1's tail deficit, the correct recommendation is 'inject less at read time' at zero collection cost, which dominates M50 and decoupled collection entirely, and the paper's headline fix is beaten by the track's own earlier finding. B1 varies *which* items are injected under coupling, not how many, so it does not cover this. A secondary omission: no arm decouples the optimizer's evaluation episodes from the bank while leaving the bank coupled at deployment, so the 2x2 confounds 'optimizer saw contracted retrievals' with 'optimizer's episodes also fed the bank'.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is above average for this track and should be credited: it names CoEvo-Mem (2608.01739) as an essentially identical mechanistic premise, refuses to minimize it, states plainly that a reviewer may read prong 1 as an adversarial test of someone else's premise, and pre-commits to what happens if CoEvo-Mem's camera-ready contains a decoupled-collection ablation. That is the right posture. It is nonetheless incomplete in three ways. It reports conclusions but no search record — no queries, date range, or venues — so its coverage cannot be judged, and it concedes no OpenReview 2026 sweep. It does not search for the one thing that decides prong 1's novelty: whether offline / memory-off experience collection already exists as a compared condition in the ExpeL and ReasoningBank lineage, where separating a collection phase from a deployment phase is closer to standard practice than to a novel control. And it does not look for the self-consuming-RAG / synthetic-corpus-loop preprint cluster beyond 2602.16136, which is where a matched-volume decoupled-corpus experiment would most plausibly already sit. Verdict on the check: honest and specific, but it establishes that the mechanism is already claimed in print and leaves novelty resting on an ablation whose absence from the literature has not actually been demonstrated.
